title: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision - Test 2

questions.q: A large block of wood of mass M=5.99 kg is hanging from two long massless cords. A bullet of mass m=10 g is fired into the block and gets embedded in it. The (block + bullet) then swing upwards, their center of mass rising a vertical distance h=9.8 cm before the (block + bullet) pendulum comes momentarily to rest at the end of its arc. The speed of the bullet just before the collision is: (Take g=9.8 m s-2)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
From energy conservation,

[after bullet gets embedded till the system comes momentarily at rest]

M+mgh=12M+mv12
[v1 is velocity after collision] 

∴ v1=2σh

Applying momentum conservation, (just before and just after collision)

mv=M+mv1

v=M+mmv1=610×10-3×2×9.8×9.8×10-2

≈831.55 m s-1

The magnitude of position vector of centre of mass of this system will be similar to the magnitude of vector :

questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
As we know, centre of mass is given by, r→com=∑mir→i∑mi

r→com=mı^+2ȷ^+k^+3m-3ı^-2ȷ^+k^m+3m

r→com=-8mı^-4mȷ^+4mk^4m=-2ı^-ȷ^+k^

questions.q: A spherical body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> is dropped from a height of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> from the ground. After hitting the ground, the body rebounds to a height of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The impulse of force imparted by the ground to the body is given by: (given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Using equation of motion with constant acceleration, we can write:

v1=2gh1 and v2=2gh2

Now, required impulse

I→=Δp→=p→f-p→i

Given, M=0.1 kg

Therefore,

I=Δp=0.1(2×9.8×5-(-2×9.8×10))

=0.1(72+14)≈2.39 kg m s-1

questions.q: The center of mass of a thin rectangular plate (fig - x ) with sides of length $a$ and $b$, whose mass per unit area $(\sigma)$ varies as $\sigma=\frac{\sigma_0 x}{a b}$ (where $\sigma_0$ is a constant), would be $\qquad$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & d m=\sigma d A \\ & \begin{aligned} d & =\sigma(d x)(d y)=\frac{\sigma_0 x}{a b}(d x)(d y) \\ x_{c o m} & =\frac{\int x d m}{\int d m}=\frac{\int x \frac{\left(\sigma_0 x\right)}{a b}(d x)(d y)}{\int_0 \frac{\sigma_0}{a b}(d x)(d y)} \\ & =\frac{\int_0^a x^2 d x \int_0^b d y}{\int_0^b x d x \int_0^b d y}=\frac{2 a}{3} \\ y_{c o m} & =\frac{\int y d m}{\int d m}=\frac{\int y\left(\frac{\sigma_0 x}{a b}\right)(d x)(d y)}{\int \frac{\sigma_0 x}{a b}(d x)(d y)}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}=\frac{\int_0^a x d x \int_0^b y d y}{\int_0^a x d x \int_0^b d y}=\frac{b}{2}$
i.e., $\vec{r}_{\mathrm{com}} \equiv\left(\frac{2 a}{3}, \frac{b}{2}\right)$

questions.q: A bullet of 10 g leaves the barrel of gun with a velocity of 600 m s-1. If the barrel of gun is 50 cm long and mass of gun is 3 kg, then value of impulse supplied to the gun will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the impulse J on the gun is given by

J=mv-u   ...1

where, m is the mass, u is the initial velocity and v is the final velocity of the bullet.

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required impulse.

J=10 g×1 kg1000 g×600-0 m s-1= 6 N s

questions.q: When kinetic energy of a body becomes 36 times of its original value, the percentage increase in the momentum of the body will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Kinetic energy $(K)=\frac{P^2}{2 m}\Rightarrow \mathrm{P}=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mK}}$
If $K_f=36 K_i$ So, $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{f}}=6 \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}\begin{aligned} \% \text { increase in momentum } & =\frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{f}}-\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}}{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}} \times 100 \% \\ & =\frac{6 \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}-\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}}{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}} \times 100 \% \\ & =500 \% \end{aligned}$

questions.q:
In two different experiments, an object of mass 5 kg moving with a speed of 25 ms-1 hits two different walls and comes to rest within
(i) 3 second, (ii) 5 seconds, respectively.
Choose the correct option out of the following :
options: Impulse and average force acting on the object will be same for both the cases.
Impulse will be same for both the cases but the average force will be different.
Average force will be same for both the cases but the impulse will be different.
Average force and impulse will be different for both the cases.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Impulse = Change in momentum

I=ΔP

Therefore, in both the cases the impulse is same.

Average force is defined as,

Favg =ΔPΔt

Since the time in the two cases is different, the average force will be different.

questions.q: A ball of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> rests on a vertical post of height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. A bullet of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math>, travelling in horizontal direction, hits the centre of the ball. After collision both travels independently. The ball hits the ground at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and the bullet at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>120</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> from the foot of the post. The value of initial velocity of the bullet will be (if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>) :
questions.subject: Physics

questions.solution:
Let initial velocity of bullet be u.

Given, mass of bullet m=10 g and mass of ball M=200 g,

Initially ball is at height 5 m and at rest, the only acceleration acting is due to gravity.

Time of flight of each ball and bullet is t=2hg.

Now, velocity of ball and bullet as v1=302hg and v2=1202hg

As the collision is elastic, so applying conservation of linear momentum.

mu+M0=Mv1+mv2

⇒0.01u=0.230g2h+0.01120g2h

⇒u=300+60=360 m s-1

An impulse of force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> is applied to end B. The time taken by the rod to turn through at right angles will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mo>,</mo></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo></math> ____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Impulse J=0.2 N s

⇒J=∫Fdt=0.2 N s

Now, angular impulse (M→) will be

Mc=∫τdt

=∫FL2dt

=L2∫Fdt=L2×J

=0.32×0.2

=0.03

Moment of inertia of the rod about the centre of mass, Icm=ML212=2×(0.3)212=0.096

Angular impulse will be equal to the change in angular momentum.

M=Icmωf-ωi

⇒0.03=0.096ωf

⇒ωf=2 rad s-1

For angular displacement, we can write θ=ωt

⇒t=θω=π2×2=π4 s.

Therefore, x=4.
